evals.prompt: We deployed an AgentCore container runtime via Terraform with a tightly scoped execution role granting `logs:CreateLogGroup`, `logs:CreateLogStream`, `logs:PutLogEvents`, and `logs:DescribeLogGroups` all restricted to `Resource: "arn:aws:logs:ap-south-1:111122223333:log-group:/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/*"`, `CMD ["python", "main.py"]`, and `print()` statements in `main.py`. Zero logs appear in CloudWatch. Identify every reason logs are missing.
evals.expected_output: Pinpoints all three causes (plus Transaction Search check): (1) **IaC IAM Trap**: `logs:DescribeLogGroups` **MUST** have `Resource: "*"` — scoping `DescribeLogGroups` to `/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/*` fails AWS IAM evaluation and silently blocks log stream creation! (2) Container `CMD` is missing the `opentelemetry-instrument` wrapper (`CMD ["opentelemetry-instrument", "python", "main.py"]`); (3) code uses `print()` instead of Python's `logging` module (OTEL log bridge captures `logging`, not bare `print()`).
expectations: Activates the agents-debug skill
Pinpoints the Terraform/CDK IAM trap: `logs:DescribeLogGroups` **must** use `Resource: "*"` (scoping it to `/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/*` silently prevents log stream creation)
Identifies both container/code causes: wrapping container startup with `opentelemetry-instrument` and replacing `print()` with Python `logging`

evals.prompt: When our upstream AWS Lambda invokes our AgentCore Runtime, two weird trace bugs happen: (1) concurrent invocations appear merged together or missing upstream context when Lambda X-Ray Active Tracing is off, and (2) when our caller passes `agentRuntimeArn="arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:ap-south-1:111122223333:runtime/order_bot/runtime-endpoint/DEFAULT"`, HTTP 200 responses come back fine but **all** child LLM/tool spans vanish! Explain both.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses both trace bugs: (1) upstream Lambda without Active Tracing (`Mode=Active` + `aws_xray_sdk` patching) propagates `Sampled=0`, causing downstream ADOT spans to drop or fail trace isolation unless Active Tracing or `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on` is configured; (2) **Endpoint ARN Trap**: passing the `/runtime-endpoint/DEFAULT` ARN to `invoke_agent_runtime` instead of the base runtime ARN (`arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:...:runtime/<name>` with `qualifier="DEFAULT"`) succeeds with HTTP 200 but drops child spans! Also notes CloudWatch span ingestion takes `~10 seconds` end-to-end.
expectations: Activates the agents-debug skill
Explains upstream `Sampled=0` propagation when Lambda Active Tracing is disabled (fixed via Lambda `Mode=Active` / `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on`)
Pinpoints the **Endpoint ARN vs Runtime ARN trap**: invoking `.../runtime/<name>/runtime-endpoint/DEFAULT` instead of `.../runtime/<name>` (with `qualifier`) returns 200 OK while dropping child spans

evals.prompt: During a 90-second Code Interpreter / multi-step tool call, our streaming `invoke_agent_runtime` client disconnects mid-response with `httpx.RemoteProtocolError` / `IncompleteRead` after ~60 seconds of silence while the tool runs. Why does the stream drop, and how do we keep SSE streams and background work alive?
evals.expected_output: Explains that intermediate load balancers / proxies drop idle HTTP streaming connections when no bytes are yielded during a long synchronous tool execution, and prescribes yielding periodic SSE heartbeat chunks (`data: {"type": "heartbeat"}\n\n`) every **~30 seconds** (using `asyncio.shield` / background task multiplexer) or offloading background work via `add_async_task` / `complete_async_task`.
expectations: Activates the agents-debug skill
Diagnoses idle streaming connection timeout during long tool calls causing `RemoteProtocolError` / `IncompleteRead`
Prescribes emitting periodic **~30-second SSE heartbeat** events (`asyncio.shield`) and/or using `add_async_task` / `complete_async_task`
